name: Tash-Rabat Caravanserai
near: There are no permanent villages in the valley — only seasonal yurt camps by the monument. The nearest large village is At-Bashy (~60 km by road, kyrgyzstanguides 2026), the town of Naryn is ~110–113 km (about 2 h). The earlier “Tash-Rabat marker in OSM at 1.3 km” is a tract (valley)/camps, not a village.
elev: About 3,100–3,200 m: too.kg — 3,100 m; thisis-kyrgyzstan and snoezelsontheroad — 3,200 m; journalofnomads — 3,000 m. The recommended label is “about 3,100 m”.
short: Tash-Rabat is a 15th-century stone caravanserai (on the site of an earlier, presumably monastic, structure of the 10th–11th centuries) at about 3,100 m in a side valley of the At-Bashy range, on the old route to the Torugart pass.
desc: Tash-Rabat is an almost square (about 33×35 m) stone building of slabstone with a central dome and 31–34 domed and vaulted rooms (24.kg says 34, thisis-kyrgyzstan — 31). Too.kg dates the caravanserai to the 15th century and notes that it was built on the remains of a monastery of the 10th–11th centuries (Buddhist or Nestorian — not firmly established). The building stands in the Kara-Koyun valley about 15 km from the Naryn — Torugart highway; in Soviet times (1970s–80s) it was cleared of rubble and restored. Since 2025–2026 a comprehensive restoration has been under way under the state programme “Koono Tarykh Syrlary” (2023–2027): a temporary metal canopy covers the monument and some areas are fenced off. Around it are seasonal yurt camps, from which hiking and horse routes depart, including to Lake Chatyr-Kol (border zone).
guide: Tash-Rabat is a rare case where a medieval caravanserai stands almost intact in the middle of an empty high-mountain valley: step under the central dome and count the side cells — there are three dozen. Look at the mysterious well-pit inside: it is thought to be a dungeon, a burial shaft or a secret passage. Spend the night in one of the yurt camps by the monument — in the evening and at dawn the valley empties, and at night at 3,100 m it is very cold even in July. In 2026 restoration is under way and the Ministry of Culture asks people to refrain from visiting — before the trip be sure to check whether they let people inside. Horse treks to Chatyr-Kol also start from here, but they require a border permit.
see: The central domed hall and 31–34 side cells; the mysterious well/shaft inside; the slabstone masonry and traces of the Soviet restoration; the Kara-Koyun valley with yurt camps and yaks; hikes onto the surrounding slopes (the “Panda Pass” viewpoint without a permit — snoezelsontheroad) and the horse route to Lake Chatyr-Kol (with a permit). In 2026 access to the interior is restricted because of the restoration.
skip: You are not ready for a long drive: from Naryn about 2 h one way, from Bishkek a whole day. In 2026 restoration is under way: if getting inside matters to you and access is not confirmed — postpone the trip. You tolerate altitude and cold nights badly — the overnight is at ~3,100 m.
diff: Easy to visit: from the parking at the camps to the building it is a few minutes on foot. The load comes from the altitude of ~3,100 m (shortness of breath, cold nights). A horse/hiking trip to Chatyr-Kol is moderate, 2 days, 22 km one way, 1,338 m of gain (journalofnomads).
when: From mid-June to mid-September the yurt camps operate (kyrgyzstanguides 2026; snoezelsontheroad: June–September); July–August are the warmest (15–20 °C in the day, frosts at night). From November to April access is difficult or impassable because of snow (journalofnomads 2026). Restoration work runs in June–August (24.kg, 2026).
hours: Restricted because of the restoration: the Ministry of Culture of Kyrgyzstan asked tourists to temporarily refrain from visiting (Kaktus/Kabar, August 2026; earlier 24.kg on 18.05.2026 reported that visitors were let in while some areas were closed). Work is in stages until 2027; they promised to announce the resumption of full access separately. In normal times there are no official hours — the key is held by the caretaker from a neighbouring yurt camp (journalofnomads, thisis-kyrgyzstan). Google Maps marked the site as temporarily closed on 03.10.2026.
daytime: Morning and evening: soft light on the stone walls and an empty valley without tour vehicles; during the day groups arrive from the Torugart highway (editorial, based on descriptions of overnight camps).
how: Along the Naryn — Torugart highway (A365) to the south; the turn to Tash-Rabat is at about the 100th km from Naryn (too.kg), then ~15 km along a side valley (kyrgyzstanguides; the last ~15 km is bumpy gravel, snoezelsontheroad). Without a car: marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek → Naryn (new bus station, 1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St., ~600 som), then a taxi from Naryn (~3,000 som one way) or a marshrutka/shared car to At-Bashy and a taxi from there.
needcar: Yes. Public transport does not run to the valley: you need your own/rented car, a taxi from Naryn or At-Bashy, or a tour (thisis-kyrgyzstan, kyrgyzstanguides 2026).
self: Yes, if you have a car: a border permit is not needed for Tash-Rabat itself (journalofnomads, thisis-kyrgyzstan, kyrgyzstanguides 2026) — it is required only for Chatyr-Kol/Kel-Suu and beyond. The 2026 limitation is the restoration: check access to the interior in advance. Cash is essential (no ATMs).
roadtype: Paved along the Naryn — Torugart highway up to the turn-off; then ~15 km along the valley — dirt/gravel, “bumpy but passable for a careful passenger car” (kyrgyzstanguides 2026; snoezelsontheroad). In winter (November–April) snowdrifts are possible.
traveltime: From Naryn about 2 h (~110–113 km) by car (thisis-kyrgyzstan, journalofnomads); from Bishkek to Naryn by marshrutka 6–7 h (kyrgyzstanguides), so from Bishkek 8–9 h with a change. From the camps to the building it is a few minutes on foot.
stay: Several yurt camps right by the monument (season ~June–September): Sabyrbek’s camp (the oldest, recommended by snoezelsontheroad and kyrgyzstanguides), Tash Rabat Yurt Camp from Nomad's Land (double $28 with breakfast, with a winter shelter), Tash-Rabat yurt camp from ak-sai.com, the “Tash-Rabat ethno-complex”. A guide to 2026 prices: 1,200–2,000 som per person with dinner and breakfast (kyrgyzstanguides, thisis-kyrgyzstan, snoezelsontheroad).
net: There is no mobile coverage or Wi-Fi in the valley (too.kg, journalofnomads 2026, thisis-kyrgyzstan, snoezelsontheroad); the operator is not specified. The nearest coverage is on the highway closer to At-Bashy/Naryn.
entry: In the normal season — 100–150 som in cash to the caretaker (journalofnomads 2026: 100 som; snoezelsontheroad and thisis-kyrgyzstan: 150 som; kyrgyzstanguides 2026: 100–150 som). No official Ministry of Culture tariff found; during the 2026 restoration entry is restricted.
transfer: Taxi Naryn → Tash-Rabat ~3,000 som (≈$35) per car one way (thisis-kyrgyzstan, journalofnomads, 2026); round trip with waiting: from Naryn 4,000–6,000 som, from At-Bashy 3,000–4,500 som (kyrgyzstanguides, 21.09.2026).
bring: Warm clothes and a hat (frosts at night even in summer at ~3,100 m), sun protection, cash in som (no ATMs or shops), a torch for the dark cells, water purification tablets or boil river water (too.kg), passport; for Chatyr-Kol — a border permit arranged in advance.
warn:
The Ministry of Culture has closed the complex to visitors until the main stages of the restoration are completed (Kaktus, 08.2026); work proceeds in stages until 2027. The yurt camps in the valley operate.

Restoration 2025–2027: the Ministry of Culture (August 2026) asks people to temporarily refrain from visiting, some areas are fenced off, machinery is working — check access before setting out. Altitude ~3,100 m — altitude sickness is possible, night frosts in summer. No phone coverage. Lake Chatyr-Kol and the area beyond Tash-Rabat are a border zone, a permit is needed (2–3 weeks to arrange); for the caravanserai itself no permit is required. An overnight in the yurts does not give the right to enter the fenced-off monument.
food: Food is served only in the yurt camps (no shops or cafes in the valley — journalofnomads): usually home-style Kyrgyz dishes included in the price of the overnight — breakfast and dinner; reviews and videos mention a Kyrgyz lunch in a yurt, as well as kumys and dairy products from local herders (editorial; check the menu at the camp).
reviews: Google Maps: 4.6/5, 344 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: there is a Tash Rabat (Naryn Province) page with reviews, the rating was not read from this environment. Typical pros — the Silk Road atmosphere, the building’s preservation, the yurt camps and the quiet of the valley; cons — a long road, a gravel approach, cold, no phone coverage and (in 2026) restrictions because of the restoration.
p.sum: Tash-Rabat is an overnight, not an hour’s stop: from Bishkek it is 8–9 h, so the base is Naryn (marshrutka 600 som or an Asman flight 2,100 som), then a taxi/car with a driver for 2 h (≈3,000 som one way, 3,000–6,000 som round trip) and a night in a yurt camp by the monument (1,200–2,000 som with dinner and breakfast; Ak-Sai — from $65). No permit is needed for Tash-Rabat itself, but in 2026 restoration is under way: in August 2026 the Ministry of Culture asked people to refrain from visiting, Google marks the site as “temporarily closed” — check access through the camp or CBT Naryn before you go. Cash is essential: no ATMs, fuel stations or phone coverage in the valley, fill up in Naryn.

p.onsite.other.0.details: In 2026 — restoration (state programme “Koono Tarykh Syrlary”, contractor Yug-Stroyservis OJSC), a canopy and fencing; on 18.05.2026 partial entry was allowed, in 08.2026 the Ministry of Culture asked people to refrain from visiting. The key is held by the caretaker from a neighbouring camp. Kaktus (08.2026): the complex is temporarily closed to visitors, machinery and workers are on site, some areas are fenced off; work is in stages until 2027; the Ministry of Culture will announce the resumption of full access separately; tour operators are advised to take the restrictions into account. p.onsite.camping: You can pitch a tent in the valley above the camps (agree with the camp owners, from whom you can buy dinner); frosts at night even in July.
p.onsite.photo_spots: The slope opposite the entrance — a frontal view of the dome and the valley; in the evening and at dawn — soft light on the slabstone; at night — stars over the dome. Note the 2025–2027 canopy in the frame.

p.iti.0.title: 1 day from Naryn
p.iti.0.plan: 07:30 depart Naryn → 08:30 Koshoy-Korgon (30 min) → 10:00 Tash-Rabat: visit (if they let people in), lunch at the camp, a walk onto the slope → 15:00 depart → 17:00 Naryn. A round-trip taxi costs 4,000–6,000 som per car.
p.iti.1.title: 2 days with a night in a yurt
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Naryn → Koshoy-Korgon → Tash-Rabat by lunchtime, a walk/horse ride around the valley, dinner and a night in a yurt, stars. Day 2: dawn at the caravanserai, a side trip onto the slope, by evening Naryn or on to Bishkek/Song-Kol.
p.iti.2.title: 3 days with Chatyr-Kol (a border permit is needed)
p.iti.2.plan: Day 1: Naryn → Tash-Rabat, night. Day 2: on horseback/on foot 21.6 km over the pass ≈3,996 m to the camp above Chatyr-Kol. Day 3: back to Tash-Rabat and Naryn. Arrange the permit 1–2 weeks ahead (tour.too.kg 3,000 som or CBT Naryn).
p.iti.3.title: Logical combinations along the route
p.iti.3.plan: Song-Kol (via Kochkor/Kalmak-Ashuu or Naryn) → Naryn → Koshoy-Korgon → Tash-Rabat → (with a permit) Chatyr-Kol / Torugart; or Naryn → Tash-Rabat → Ak-Say valley/Kel-Suu with a permit.
p.season: May: snow on the slopes, camps not yet open, nights −5…0 °C. Mid-June — mid-September: yurt season, +15…20 °C in the day, frosts at night; July–August — peak of tourist groups. Restoration work — June–August (2025–2027). Late September — October: camps wind down, first snow. November — April: the valley is snowed in, access is difficult or impossible.
p.budget.economy: ≈6,500–8,000 som per person for 2 days from Bishkek: marshrutka Bishkek — Naryn round trip 1,200; taxi Naryn — Tash-Rabat round trip 4,000–6,000 per car (≈1,500–2,000 per person in a group of 3–4); a yurt with half board 1,200–2,000; entry 100–150; a night in Naryn 1,500–2,500.
p.budget.comfort: ≈25,000–45,000 som per person: Asman flight 2×2,100, car with driver/tour (Eurasia Travel from $500 for 2 days), Ak-Sai $75–85 with full board, horse 1,500 + guide 2,500 som/day.
p.permits: No border permit is needed for the caravanserai itself. It is needed for Chatyr-Kol, Kel-Suu, Ak-Say and Arpa (the border zone of the At-Bashy district): tour.too.kg — 3,000 som, 5–7 working days, office at 105/3 Isanov St., Bishkek; or via CBT Naryn (€30, urgent €50 in 2 days). It is checked at military posts; the original + passport are needed. Entry to the monument — 100–150 som to the caretaker (in 2026 access is restricted by the restoration).
p.access: With children — yes, if the child tolerates the altitude of ~3,100 m and cold nights; for older people — a short visit is possible (a few minutes over uneven ground from the parking), but altitude and cold are a risk factor. Stroller — no (gravel, steps, uneven floor). With a dog — animals are allowed at the Omurbek camps per the description; inside the monument — no.
